title: Defend the peg

controls.label: Fall in demand (billion units a year)

x.label: Quantity of currency (billion units a year)

readouts.l: Gap at the peg (bought each year)

predict.q: The peg is 0.50 US dollars per unit. The central bank has 30 billion US dollars of reserves. Demand for the currency falls by 20 billion units a year at every price. What must the central bank do to hold the peg?

options.s: Sell its own currency, to calm the market.
options.fb: Selling adds to supply and widens the gap at the peg.

options.s: Buy its own currency with its dollar reserves.
options.fb: It buys the 20 billion units of excess supply at 0.50, spending 10 billion US$ a year: the reserves last 3 years.

options.s: Cut interest rates, to support the economy.
options.fb: A rate cut causes outflows, so demand for the currency falls further.

options.s: Nothing: the peg is set by law, so the price cannot move.
options.fb: A peg is a promise, not a law of the market; without intervention the rate falls to 0.45.

task: Move the demand fall slider to 20 and watch the gap at the peg, the reserves spent each year and how many years they last. Switch on "raise interest rates" and watch the gap shrink.

target.do: Move the demand fall slider to 20, then press Check.

takeaway: A peg under downward pressure lasts as long as the reserves, and the willingness to keep interest rates high.
